label: Bible Study
prompt: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his _____ over me was love.
verse: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
note: The banqueting house verse — a favorite Sunday school chorus with a love banner flying high.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good _____; it is I; be not afraid.
verse: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
note: Spoken across the waves to terrified disciples at night — moments before Peter steps out of the boat.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a _____: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
verse: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
note: Mid-storm, Jesus was asleep on a pillow in the back of the boat — only Mark mentions the pillow.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For the word of God is _____, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
verse: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
note: 'Quick' is KJV for living, as in 'the quick and the dead' — Scripture is alive and cuts deeper than steel.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and _____ with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
verse: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
note: 'A man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief' — the line Handel set in Messiah's aria 'He was despised.'
